events.title: Symfony 3.0 released
events.summary: Symfony 3.0 shipped on November 30, 2015 — simplifying the framework with fewer core bundles and a cleaner directory structure.
events.about: Symfony 3 trimmed legacy bundles into standalone components and tightened the full-stack framework for PHP 5.5+. It powered Laravel's HttpFoundation, Drupal 8+, and enterprise APIs — setting patterns for dependency injection and [HTTP] abstractions across PHP.

narrative.whyChosen: Symfony 3 modernized the framework that shaped PHP's component ecosystem.
narrative.whyImportant: Standalone components let teams adopt Symfony pieces without the full stack.
narrative.problemSolved: Symfony 2 carried bundle sprawl and legacy paths that confused new adopters.

events.title: Raspberry Pi Zero released
events.summary: The Raspberry Pi Foundation released the Pi Zero on November 26, 2015 — a $5 [single-board computer] the size of a stick of gum.
events.about: The Zero trimmed GPIO and ports to hit a five-dollar price — makers embedded it in drones, wearables, and IoT prototypes where a full Pi was overkill. It ran the same Linux userspace as the Model B, so Python and GPIO code ported easily. The Zero W later added Wi-Fi for headless projects.

narrative.whyChosen: The Pi Zero made embedded Linux almost disposable-cheap for hobby and production prototypes.
narrative.whyImportant: It extended the Raspberry Pi ecosystem into ultra-compact and cost-sensitive projects.
narrative.problemSolved: Makers needed a full Linux board smaller and cheaper than the $35 Model B for embedded builds.

events.title: TensorFlow open sourced
events.summary: Google open sourced TensorFlow on November 9, 2015 — a [machine learning] framework for training and deploying [neural network]s at scale.
events.about: TensorFlow (`tf.keras`, computational graphs, TPU support) replaced Google's internal DistBelief stack and became the default ML toolkit for researchers and production teams. It powers recommendation, vision, and [NLP] systems — though PyTorch later challenged it in research.

narrative.whyChosen: TensorFlow democratized Google's production ML infrastructure for the wider community.
narrative.whyImportant: It standardized how teams build, train, and deploy [deep learning] models.
narrative.problemSolved: Researchers lacked portable tools matching the scale and reliability of hyperscaler ML systems.

events.title: Drupal 8 released
events.summary: Drupal 8.0 shipped on November 19, 2015 — rebuilding core on Symfony components with REST APIs and configuration management.
events.about: Drupal 8 replaced procedural hooks with [OOP] services, Twig templates, and Symfony's [HTTP] [kernel] — a five-year rewrite that aligned Drupal with modern PHP. It added JSON APIs and CMI for deploying config between environments, setting the foundation for Drupal 9/10.

narrative.whyChosen: Drupal 8 was the Symfony modernization that kept Drupal relevant in enterprise PHP.
narrative.whyImportant: It brought REST-first architecture and composer-based workflows to a major CMS.
narrative.problemSolved: Drupal 7's legacy architecture could not match modern PHP frameworks and [API] expectations.

events.title: Magento 2.0 released
events.summary: Magento Commerce released Magento 2.0 on November 17, 2015 — a full re-architecture with dependency injection, Composer, and a new admin [UI].
events.about: Magento 2 replaced the 1.x codebase with modular PHP, DI containers, and improved caching — a painful but necessary migration for enterprise e-commerce. It introduced new checkout flows, Page Builder (later), and the path to Adobe Commerce after Adobe's acquisition.

narrative.whyChosen: Magento 2 was the platform rewrite merchants needed for modern PHP commerce.
narrative.whyImportant: Dependency injection and Composer aligned Magento with enterprise PHP practices.
narrative.problemSolved: Magento 1's legacy architecture could not meet performance and extensibility demands at scale.

events.title: Jamstack term coined
events.summary: Matt Biilmann published "What is the JAMstack?" on November 16, 2015 — naming the JavaScript, APIs, and Markup architecture Netlify had been enabling.
events.about: Jamstack described pre-rendered sites served from CDNs with serverless APIs — decoupling the frontend from monolithic backends. The term gave a vocabulary to static site generators, headless CMSs, and Git-based deploy workflows that defined modern web development.

narrative.whyChosen: Jamstack named the architectural shift from LAMP monoliths to composable frontends.
narrative.whyImportant: It unified static generators, headless CMSs, and CDN deploys under one movement.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams building decoupled sites lacked a shared term to describe their approach.

events.title: ERC-20 token standard finalized
events.summary: EIP-20 finalized the ERC-20 fungible token interface on November 19, 2015 — standardizing `transfer`, `approve`, and `balanceOf` for Ethereum tokens.
events.about: ERC-20 let exchanges, wallets, and [DeFi] protocols integrate any compliant token without custom code. The 2017 ICO wave minted thousands of ERC-20 assets; Uniswap pools and MetaMask balances all assume this ABI. It became the template every EVM chain copied.

narrative.whyChosen: ERC-20 standardized how fungible assets work on Ethereum.
narrative.whyImportant: A common interface unlocked composable [DeFi] and exchange integrations.
narrative.problemSolved: Every token contract used incompatible APIs, blocking wallets and automated market makers.
